title: Pending approvals count and list do not match the role's real review queue
evidence: Ask AI: `if ($role === 'SUPER_ADMIN') { $approvalsQuery->where('required_role', 'SUPER_ADMIN'); } elseif ($role === 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD') { ...->where('required_role', 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD')->whereIn('organization_id', $orgIds); } else { $approvalsQuery->where('organization_id', (int) $user->organization_id); }`. The real queue (ApprovalRequestController::scopeToAwaiting, lines 158-171) uses `where('required_role', $user->approvalRole())` and `whereNull('assigned_approver')->orWhere('assigned_approver', $user->school_id)`, and for the SAO it limits to `superAdminReviewableEntityTypes()` or unified budget/election rows of university-wide orgs. `index()` also returns 403 for SBO_OFFICER unless scope=submitted (line 69). pending_approvals is not in INTENT_MODULES, so module limits do not apply either.
impact: An org Admin is told "N pending approval request(s) currently in your queue" when N counts requests that wait on the Dean or the SAO. An SBO Officer, who cannot open the approvals queue at all, gets every pending request in the org with requester names, including student payment approvals. The SAO and the Dean get counts that include rows assigned to another approver or entity types they cannot review.
suggested_fix: Build the query the way scopeToAwaiting does. Use `where('required_role', $user->approvalRole())` and the assigned_approver clause, keep the SAO entity-type/unified rule (move it into a shared scope on ApprovalRequest that both callers use), and use `whereIn('organization_id', $organizationIds)` for non-SAO roles. For SBO_OFFICER, return the 'Not available' payload, or show only their own submitted requests (scopeToSubmitted).
verifier_notes: buildPendingApprovals (now line ~1651) filters required_role only for SAO/Dean and, for every other role, takes all pending rows of the org with no required_role, no assigned_approver clause and no SAO entity-type rule; scopeToAwaiting (ApprovalRequestController ~158) does all three, and index() returns 403 to SBO_OFFICER without scope=submitted. pending_approvals is absent from INTENT_MODULES and STUDENT_INTENTS gating does not cover SBO, so SBO officers reach it.

title: SAO missing-submissions view counts pending, returned and archived organizations
evidence: `$orgs = Organization::whereIn('id', $organizationIds)->orderBy('name')->get(['id', 'name', 'acronym', 'lifecycle_status']);` and lifecycle_status is never read afterwards. The id list comes from `scopedStudentOrganizationIds()` (line 2386): `DB::table('organizations')->where('organization_type', 'STUDENT_ORGANIZATION')->pluck('id')`, with no lifecycle filter. The compliance page (ComplianceController::status, lines 381/387) uses only `where('lifecycle_status', 'active')`.
impact: The Dean and the SAO are told that archived (read-only) organizations and organizations still in registration are 'Missing files' or 'Overdue' on financial reports. 'Out of %d student organization(s) in scope' and 'Fully submitted orgs' disagree with the compliance page, which is the main question the dean asks.
suggested_fix: Add `->where('lifecycle_status', 'active')` to the `$orgs` query. Use `$orgs->pluck('id')` (not the raw `$organizationIds`) for the submissions and financial_reports queries so every count shares one denominator.
verifier_notes: scopedStudentOrganizationIds() for SAO plucks every STUDENT_ORGANIZATION, and User::scopedOrganizationIds() for the Dean uses Organization::student()->where('college_id') with no lifecycle filter; the $orgs query (~1303) selects lifecycle_status but never filters on it. ComplianceController::status uses where('lifecycle_status','active').

title: Missing financial report count is capped at 12
evidence: `foreach ($orgsMissingReport->take(self::ROW_LIMIT) as $org) { $missingReportRows[] = [...]; }` followed by `$missingReportTotal = count($missingReportRows);` (line 1295). ROW_LIMIT is 12. That total feeds the answer sentence ('%d organization(s) have not yet submitted against the latest deadline') and the 'Missing financial reports' highlight.
impact: With 30 organizations missing the report, the SAO is told 12. The headline number is wrong whenever more than 12 organizations are late.
suggested_fix: Set `$missingReportTotal = $orgsMissingReport->count();` before taking rows, and keep `take(self::ROW_LIMIT)` only for the rows.
verifier_notes: $missingReportTotal = count($missingReportRows) (~1389) after foreach over $orgsMissingReport->take(ROW_LIMIT); answer and highlight use it, so the total is capped at 12.

title: Event file check filters on statuses that do not exist and skips planning events
evidence: `Event::where('organization_id', $orgId)->whereIn('status', ['draft', 'pending', 'approved'])`. The events status enum is `['planning', 'approved', 'ongoing', 'completed', 'cancelled']` (create_events_table migration line 21; EventController validates `in:planning,approved,ongoing,completed,cancelled`).
impact: Events in 'planning', where proposal files are still being gathered before approval, are never checked. Only already-approved events are. An Admin asking what event files are missing gets 0 for the events that need them most.
suggested_fix: Use `whereIn('status', ['planning', 'approved'])`, or add 'ongoing' too if requirements still apply then, and keep the end_time/semester filter so old events drop out.
verifier_notes: Org branch (~1445) uses whereIn('status',['draft','pending','approved']); events enum is planning/approved/ongoing/completed/cancelled and no later migration changes it, so planning events are never checked.
corrected_fix: Use whereIn('status', ['planning', 'approved']). There is currently no end_time or semester filter to keep: add one (for example where('end_time', '>=', now()) or the active semester) so past approved events stop filling the 8-event window.

title: Clearance queue counts lines of other signatory roles
evidence: `} elseif ($role === 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD') { $query->whereIn('clearance_signatures.organization_id', $organizationIds->all()); } else { $query->where('clearance_signatures.organization_id', (int) $user->organization_id); }`. ClearanceController::signaturesIndex (lines 248-252) adds `where('required_role', 'department_head')` for the Dean and `where('required_role', 'organization')` for Admin/Officer, and canSign only lets each role sign its own line.
impact: The Dean and org officers are told 'N pending clearance signature(s) ... in your queue' and listed students whose pending line is really the SAO's or another signatory's. They open the clearances page and cannot find or sign them.
suggested_fix: Add `->where('clearance_signatures.required_role', 'department_head')` in the DEPARTMENT_HEAD branch and `->where('clearance_signatures.required_role', 'organization')` in the org branch, matching signaturesIndex.
verifier_notes: ClearanceController::store inserts one row per required role with the student's organization_id for every role (sao, department_head, organization), so the Ask AI Dean branch (whereIn organization_id) and org branch (where organization_id) count SAO and other-role lines. signaturesIndex filters required_role 'department_head' / 'organization'.

title: Student elections answer shows unfinalized or cancelled elections and misses organizations the student votes in
evidence: `$orgIds = in_array($role, ['SUPER_ADMIN', 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD'], true) ? $organizationIds->all() : [(int) $user->organization_id];` then `->whereIn('elections.status', ['active', 'upcoming'])`, with no finalized_at or cancelled_at check. ElectionController::index (lines 224, 242-247) scopes students to `$user->electionOrganizationIds()` (votingOrganizationIds: college home plus every org with a voting profile) and only shows `whereNull('cancelled_at')` and `whereIn('status', ['upcoming','active'])->whereNotNull('finalized_at')`.
impact: Students and member-view officers see the titles and close times of elections that were approved but never finalized, or were cancelled. A student on a college profile is told there are no elections even when college-wide or org elections they can vote in are active. The 'Open election' link goes to cast-vote for an upcoming election that cannot be voted in yet.
suggested_fix: Use `$user->electionOrganizationIds()` for STUDENT and member-view roles. Add `whereNull('elections.cancelled_at')`, plus `whereNotNull('elections.finalized_at')` for those viewers. Link upcoming rows to '/dashboard/elections/election-info' and only active rows to cast-vote.
verifier_notes: Scope and finalization parts are real: students/members use [organization_id] instead of electionOrganizationIds(), and there is no finalized_at check, while approved-but-unfinalized elections sit at status 'upcoming' with finalized_at null (ElectionController ~707). The cancelled part is wrong: ElectionGovernanceController sets status 'closed' together with cancelled_at, so a cancelled election never matches whereIn('status',['active','upcoming']).
corrected_fix: For STUDENT and member-view roles use $user->electionOrganizationIds() and add whereNotNull('elections.finalized_at') (optionally whereNull('elections.suspended_at')); no cancelled_at filter is needed. Link upcoming rows to '/dashboard/elections/election-info' and only active rows to cast-vote.

title: Compliance 'missing' list mixes renewal and semestral-report categories
evidence: `ComplianceRequirementType::where('academic_year', $academicYear)->where('is_active', true)->where(fn ($q) => ...)` has no category filter. The same is true in missingComplianceRequirementsForOrganization (line 2345). AccreditationStatusService::forOrganizations (line 44) and ComplianceController::status (line 397) both filter `where('category', 'organization')` by default, and renewal requirements belong to incoming officers (ComplianceController line 514).
impact: Ask AI says an organization is 'Missing files', or counts '0 fully submitted orgs', while the compliance page and the accreditation badge say it is complete, because renewal and semestral-report items are counted as outstanding organization requirements.
suggested_fix: Add `->where('category', 'organization')` to both queries, or group rows by category and label each one ('Renewal', 'Semestral report') so the totals match the compliance page.
verifier_notes: Both requirement-type queries (~1295 and missingComplianceRequirementsForOrganization ~2445) lack a category filter; AccreditationStatusService line 44 and ComplianceController::status line 397 default to category 'organization', and renewal uploads are refused to outgoing officers (ComplianceController ~514).

title: Hard-coded compliance link sends SBO Officers to a route they cannot open
evidence: `'href' => '/dashboard/compliance',` is a literal and is not passed through `$this->routeAccess->hrefFor()`. App.jsx line 381: `<Route path="compliance" element={<ProtectedRoute allowedRoles={["ADMIN"]}>`. client_routes.php SBO_OFFICER has no '/dashboard/compliance'. The helper feeds buildMissingSubmissions (line 1347) for ADMIN and SBO_OFFICER, and daily priorities (line 1069).
impact: An officer clicks 'Upload' and is redirected away. This breaks the client_routes allowlist contract that ClientRouteAllowlistTest is meant to enforce.
suggested_fix: Pass the role into the helper and use `'href' => $this->routeAccess->hrefFor($role, '/dashboard/compliance')` so roles without the route get null.
verifier_notes: missingComplianceRequirementsForOrganization hard-codes 'href' => '/dashboard/compliance'; buildMissingSubmissions org branch returns these rows to SBO_OFFICER (compliance module allowed by default), while App.jsx limits compliance to ADMIN and client_routes SBO_OFFICER lacks it. No later step filters payload hrefs. Daily priorities only uses the count from this helper and its own row uses hrefFor, so that part of the evidence does not apply.

title: Dean's office staff get links to Department Head-only routes
evidence: UseAccountProfile calls `activateProfile($profile, signedInRequest: true)`, and User::getRoleAttribute returns 'DEPARTMENT_HEAD' for college office staff, so `$role` here is DEPARTMENT_HEAD and hrefFor checks the DEPARTMENT_HEAD list. The builders then return `'/dashboard/department-head/compliance'` (lines 1288, 1468, 1507). The client sees the stored role 'ADMIN' (attributesToArray line 142), and App.jsx line 291 allows that route only for `["DEPARTMENT_HEAD"]`. client_routes ADMIN does not list it.
impact: The dean's delegate clicks 'View reports' or 'View file' and is redirected away from the page.
suggested_fix: Resolve hrefs against the client-facing role, `$user->profileRole()`, not `$user->role`. Or open department-head/compliance to ADMIN behind OfficeReviewRoute in App.jsx and client_routes together.
verifier_notes: UseAccountProfile calls activateProfile(..., signedInRequest: true), so getRoleAttribute returns DEPARTMENT_HEAD for college office staff while attributesToArray sends 'ADMIN' to the client. App.jsx department-head/compliance allows only DEPARTMENT_HEAD and client_routes ADMIN lacks it, so links resolved against DEPARTMENT_HEAD redirect office staff.

title: SAO approvals link points to the compliance page instead of the approvals queue
evidence: `'href' => $this->routeAccess->hrefFor($role, $role === 'SUPER_ADMIN' ? '/dashboard/super-admin/compliance' : '/dashboard/approvals'),`. The SAO reviews ApprovalRequests at '/dashboard/super-admin/organization-approvals' (App.jsx line 315 renders DepartmentHeadApprovalsPage there; HowToGuideLibrary lines 204-206 and UX_FLOW.md line 289 name it 'Approvals').
impact: Every 'Review' button in the SAO pending-approval list opens the compliance page, where the request is not shown.
suggested_fix: Use '/dashboard/super-admin/organization-approvals' for SUPER_ADMIN rows.
verifier_notes: Row href uses '/dashboard/super-admin/compliance' for SUPER_ADMIN; App.jsx line 315 renders DepartmentHeadApprovalsPage at super-admin/organization-approvals, which is in client_routes SUPER_ADMIN.

title: Open invoice count includes cancelled and waived invoices
evidence: `DB::table('invoices')->whereIn('organization_id', $orgIds)->where('status', '!=', 'paid')->count();`. StudentAccountBalances (line 32) treats open as `whereNotIn('status', ['paid', 'cancelled', 'waived'])`, and Invoice.php line 28 marks cancelled/waived as closed. The student list (line 1861) also gives cancelled/waived rows the 'warning' tone.
impact: 'there are %d unpaid student invoice(s)' overstates collections for Admins, Deans and the SAO. Students see a waived fee flagged as something they still owe.
suggested_fix: Use `->whereNotIn('status', ['paid', 'cancelled', 'waived'])`. In the student rows, set the tone to 'neutral' for cancelled/waived.
verifier_notes: Invoice count uses where('status','!=','paid'); StudentAccountBalances uses whereNotIn paid/cancelled/waived and Invoice::isVoided treats cancelled/waived as not owed. Student rows tone every non-paid status 'warning'.

title: Low-budget tone uses remaining vs allocated, which income hides
evidence: `'status_tone' => ((float) $b->remaining_amount <= ((float) $b->allocated_amount * 0.15)) ? 'warning' : 'success'`. BudgetController line 141 sets remaining = allocated + income - spent. DashboardBriefingService (lines 456-462, 794-799) flags budgets by summed expense transactions per budget: 'Income posted against a budget raises its remaining amount above what was allocated, so spending is summed per budget'.
impact: A budget that spent 95% of its allocation but got income shows green 'success' in Ask AI while the dashboard flags it. The two surfaces disagree on the same budget.
suggested_fix: Load per-budget expense sums: `DB::table('transactions')->whereIn('budget_id', $approvedBudgets->pluck('id'))->where('type','expense')->groupBy('budget_id')->selectRaw('budget_id, SUM(amount) spent')`. Tone by spent/allocated >= 80%, like the dashboard, and show spent next to remaining.
verifier_notes: BudgetController line 141 sets remaining = allocated + income - spent and TransactionController adds deltas, so income lifts remaining; the tone uses remaining <= 15% of allocated, while DashboardBriefingService flags utilization >= 80% from summed spending, as the project's budget rule requires.

title: Several counts are taken after limit(12) and are capped
evidence: Events: `->limit(self::ROW_LIMIT)->get(...)` then `$upcomingEvents->count()` in the answer and highlight (2062, 2066). Elections: `->limit(self::ROW_LIMIT)` then `$elections->where('status','active')->count()` (2248, 2253). Grievances: `->limit(self::ROW_LIMIT)` then `$openGrievances->count()` and `$urgentCount` (2299, 2304). Submitted reports: `->limit(self::ROW_LIMIT)` then `$reports->count()` (1518, 1527).
impact: The SAO with 40 open grievances is told 'There are 12 unresolved grievance(s)'. A Dean with 20 upcoming college events is told 12. The active/upcoming election split comes from the 12 soonest rows only.
suggested_fix: Run a separate `(clone $query)->count()` (and grouped counts for status or urgency) before applying limit, as buildTasksWorkload already does, and use those totals in the answer and highlights.
verifier_notes: Events (upcomingEvents->count()), elections (active/upcoming split), grievances (count and urgentCount) and financial reports ($reports->count()) are all computed from collections already limited to ROW_LIMIT, unlike buildTasksWorkload which counts before limiting.

title: Grievance queue includes soft-deleted grievances
evidence: `DB::table('grievances')->whereNotIn('status', ['resolved', 'dismissed'])`. The grievances table has softDeletes (2026_10_13_000004 migration) and Grievance uses SoftDeletes, but the query builder ignores the scope. GrievanceController::show returns 404 for trashed grievances to non-students (line 91).
impact: Grievances a student withdrew or deleted still appear in the SAO's Ask AI queue and counts, even though the SAO can no longer open them.
suggested_fix: Add `->whereNull('deleted_at')` (or use `Grievance::query()`), and count before the limit (see askai-builders-13).
verifier_notes: Grievances table has softDeletes (2026_10_13_000004) and the builder uses DB::table('grievances') without whereNull('deleted_at'); GrievanceController::show 404s trashed grievances for non-students.

title: Builders ignore the semester for tasks, events, budgets and elections
evidence: Tasks (1747-1750), events (2033-2037, 2050-2054), budgets (1879-1898) and elections (2233-2236) have no academic_semester_id or SemesterScope filter. TaskController line 66-68 and EventController line 74-76 filter on `AcademicSemester::selected($request)`. BudgetController line 38 uses `SemesterScope::budgets(...)`, and ElectionController lines 231-235 filters by the selected semester.
impact: After a rollover, Ask AI keeps counting the previous semester's overdue tasks, stale 'needs closing' events and the whole history of approved budget allocations. Its answers disagree with the pages its links open, and money totals cover several years.
suggested_fix: Resolve `$semester = AcademicSemester::active()` once in answer(), or selected() if the request is passed in. Apply `where('academic_semester_id', $semester->id)` to tasks/events/elections (keeping rows with a null semester, as ElectionController does) and `SemesterScope::budgets` for budgets.
verifier_notes: tasks, events and elections have academic_semester_id, and TaskController/EventController/ElectionController filter by the selected semester; the Ask AI builders (tasks, events, budgets, elections, daily priorities) have no semester filter.
corrected_fix: Resolve AcademicSemester::active() once and filter tasks/events/elections by academic_semester_id (keep null rows for elections as ElectionController does). SemesterScope::budgets takes an Eloquent builder (it uses whereHas('event')), so the budget rows and totals must switch from DB::table('budgets') to Budget::query() before applying it.

title: Org-scoped 'what haven't we submitted' never checks financial reports
evidence: The ADMIN/SBO branch builds only `$missingCompliance` and `$missingEventReqRows`. The financial_report_deadlines check (lines 1269-1292) runs only in the SUPER_ADMIN/DEPARTMENT_HEAD branch, yet the follow-up asks "What compliance requirements, event files, or reports haven't we submitted?" (line 1182).
impact: An org Admin whose financial report is overdue is told nothing about it by the intent that promises to cover reports. The dean's top accountability item cannot be checked by the organization that has to submit it.
suggested_fix: In the org branch, run the same latest-deadline check for `$orgId`. Add a 'Financial report' section and highlight linked to `hrefFor($role, '/dashboard/finance/financial-ledger')`, or to the report page the org uses.
verifier_notes: The ADMIN/SBO branch of buildMissingSubmissions only checks compliance and event files; the financial_report_deadlines check runs only in the SAO/Dean branch, while the daily-priorities follow-up asks about reports.

title: Merchandise 'pending verification' counts orders without proof, and the row copy contradicts itself
evidence: `$pendingVerify = (clone $query)->where('orders.status', 'pending')->count();` and the row `'status' => $ord->status === 'paid' ? 'Ready to claim' : 'Pending verification'` with secondary `($ord->payment_proof_url ? 'Payment proof uploaded' : 'Awaiting payment proof')`. DashboardBriefingService::ordersToVerifyAttention (lines 594-598) counts only `officer_review_status = 'pending'` orders whose GCash proof is in.
impact: Officers are told N orders await their verification when many still have no proof or were already officer-reviewed. Each such row reads 'Pending verification' and 'Awaiting payment proof' at once.
suggested_fix: Split the counts. 'Awaiting verification' uses the dashboard's officer_review_status/payment-proof predicate. 'Awaiting payment' covers pending orders without proof. Set the row status to 'Awaiting payment' when no proof is uploaded.
verifier_notes: $pendingVerify counts every pending order, while daily priorities in the same service and DashboardBriefingService::ordersToVerifyAttention count status pending + officer_review_status pending + proof present; the row shows 'Pending verification' with 'Awaiting payment proof' for orders without proof.

title: 'Submitted financial reports' count includes rejected reports
evidence: `->whereIn('financial_reports.submission_status', ['pending_department_head', 'pending_sao', 'approved', 'rejected'])` and the answer: `'... along with %d submitted financial report(s).', ..., $reports->count()`, plus the highlight 'Submitted financial reports'.
impact: Rejected reports that need resubmission are reported as submitted, so the Dean overestimates how many organizations have complied.
suggested_fix: Count pending and approved separately from rejected (for example 'N awaiting review, M approved, K returned'), using unlimited counts.
verifier_notes: The answer and highlight call rejected reports 'submitted', which disagrees with buildMissingSubmissions where rejected does not count as covered, and the count is capped at 12 (see 13). The impact overstates: the count is of reports, not organizations, and each row shows a 'Rejected' badge.

title: Merchandise answer for SAO or Dean reads the office's own organization
evidence: `$orgId = (int) $user->organization_id; $query = DB::table('orders')...->where('orders.organization_id', $orgId);`. buildMerchandiseOrders takes no `$organizationIds`, and intentAllowed lets SUPER_ADMIN and DEPARTMENT_HEAD reach it ('order', 'claim' keywords).
impact: The SAO or the Dean is told 'There are 0 pending order(s)' for the agency or college home organization, which looks like an authoritative zero for the student organizations.
suggested_fix: For SUPER_ADMIN/DEPARTMENT_HEAD, either use `whereIn('orders.organization_id', $organizationIds)` with an org column in the rows, or return the 'Not available' payload, since neither role manages orders.
verifier_notes: buildMerchandiseOrders takes no organization scope and uses $user->organization_id; classifyIntent routes 'order'/'claim' questions to merchandise_orders for any role and moduleAllowed is true for non-SBO roles, so the SAO or Dean gets counts for the agency or college home organization.

title: Queries inside loops for event requirement files and approval labels
evidence: `foreach ($upcomingOrDraftEvents as $event) { $activeReqs = EventRequirement::activeForEvent($event)->...->get(); $uploadedReqIds = EventRequirementFile::where('event_id', $event->id)...->pluck(...); }` runs 2 queries per event. In buildPendingApprovals, `$this->entityLabels->for($req)` (line 1582) runs one entity query per row.
impact: About 16 extra queries per missing-submissions answer and 12 per approvals answer, on a throttled interactive endpoint.
suggested_fix: Load EventRequirementFile rows for all event ids at once and group by event_id. Batch approval labels by entity_type with one whereIn per type.
verifier_notes: The org branch runs EventRequirement::activeForEvent and EventRequirementFile queries per event (up to 8 events), and ApprovalEntityLabel::for runs one find() per approval row (up to 12).
